title: Code Reviewer capability probe, version 1
description: The capability probe of the hosted deployment (#316, #331). ProbeVerdict is the one line of JSON that the Worker image prints in its `probe` entry mode (#324, runner/README.md): which engines the container may advertise and, when `opencode` is not among them, the stable reasons of its startup self-check (docs/dynamic-review.md, 'The startup self-check'). It holds engines and stable reasons and nothing else: no path, no value of the environment, no text. The Dispatcher runs the probe in a canary VM from the golden snapshot with the flags of the hardened container spec, only when the deploy canary asks (`POST /probe`); the dispatch path runs no probe (#479). A deployment goes live only after a canary whose verdict passed (fail closed). ProbeReport is what `POST /probe` of the Dispatcher answers (authorized with the dispatcher credential as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`): the verdict as the Dispatcher read it, or the stable code of the reason no verdict was read. It is what a deploy step reads to block a release whose Dynamic canary fails. A reader ignores fields it does not know; the writer of a ProbeVerdict never adds one.

ProbeEngine.description: An engine a container may advertise: `pr-agent` runs Diff jobs, `opencode` runs Dynamic jobs, `implementer` runs the Implementer's turns (#765; only a container of the Implementer's profile, with its work volume, advertises it, and only after the Dynamic self-check and its own passed).

ProbeReason.description: Why an engine is not advertised: the `SelfCheckReason` values of the runner (runner/src/code_reviewer_runner/dynamic_review/self_check.py). The `implementer_*` ones say why `implementer` is missing from a container whose Dynamic self-check passed (#765); every other one says why `opencode` is. `implementer_probe_failed` is written by the Dispatcher's canary, never by the runner: the Implementer's half of its probe did not run, was not a verdict, or failed a check of the Dynamic self-check in its container, so `implementer` is missing while the Dynamic verdict stands. A closed set, so that the Dispatcher can keep a verdict to stable reasons and drop anything else. Both ends check their lists against this one.

ProbeVerdict.description: The line the `probe` mode prints. `engines` always holds `pr-agent`; `opencode` is in it only when the whole self-check passed (the hardening of the container, the egress mode, IPv6 off where the fallback ruleset needs it, the pins), and then `reasons` holds no reason against it. `implementer` (#765) is in it only in a container of the Implementer's profile, on top of `opencode`, when its own start-up check passed as well (git and setpriv, the work volume prepared and exec-capable, the network rules); a container whose own check failed has `opencode` and the `implementer_*` reasons. A container that is no Implementer container has no such reason.

ProbeStatus.description: `passed`: the canary container answered and advertises `opencode`. `denied`: it answered and does not (the reasons say why). `failed`: no verdict was read (the canary VM, the container or the clock failed); `failure` says which.

ProbeFailure.description: Why no verdict was read: a closed list of stable codes, the launch codes of a job VM and the codes of the probe itself. The Dispatcher keeps the list in dispatcher/src/probe/failure-codes.ts (a test holds them equal); a code that is not on it is probe_error.

ProbeReport.description: The answer of `POST /probe`: 200 when every engine the Dispatcher is configured to serve is advertised (`ok` true), 503 with the same body when one is not. `engines` and `reasons` are what the Dispatcher advertises and why not; `failure` is a code of the closed `ProbeFailure` list, present only for `failed`. 401 with the runner API's ErrorResponse, the same for every refusal, when the credential is missing or wrong; no VM is created then.

required.description: The engines this Dispatcher required for `ok`: those of the reviewer kinds, and `implementer` only once the Launcher advertises it. A deploy step names the ones `engines` lacks when it blocks. It may hold `implementer`, which `engines` holds only when the canary proved the Implementer's container too.

snapshotId.description: The golden snapshot this deployment creates job VMs from (`SANDBOX_SNAPSHOT_ID`), present when one is configured. With `imageDigest` it names the whole pair, so that a deploy step can tell that the deployment runs the snapshot its pipeline built, also when a rebuild left the image id unchanged (#403).

imageDigest.description: The id of the Worker image this deployment is configured with (`SANDBOX_IMAGE_DIGEST`), present when one is configured. A deploy step compares it with the image its pipeline built, so that a canary that passed is known to have proven that image (#403).
